principles: Keep one canonical policy source and sync neighboring docs to it.
Keep low-risk audit buckets narrow: wording-only, annotation-compliance, and pure typo cleanups only.
Preserve the stronger three-round two-host rule for lifecycle, gate, Authority, and process-fact work.
drivers: User needs the low-risk one-round policy to be explicit and easy to read.
Current wording is split across runbooks instead of one canonical decision doc.
The change must not alter runtime gate behavior or Authority Server semantics.

options.name: A: Canonicalize the low-risk bucket in story-lifecycle.md and sync the runbooks
pros: Creates one source of truth for the one-round policy.
Lets the adjacent runbooks reference the same rule instead of drifting.
Makes the narrow low-risk bucket explicit without touching runtime code.
cons: Touches the canonical policy doc, so the wording must be precise.
Requires coordinated doc sync across the related decision docs.

options.name: B: Leave story-lifecycle.md unchanged and only add more exceptions in the runbooks
cons: The policy stays split across multiple places and stays easy to misread.
Drift remains likely because the canonical doc would still not carry the rule.
The story still looks like a wording patch instead of a coherent policy fix.

chosen: A: Canonicalize the low-risk bucket in story-lifecycle.md and sync the runbooks
rationale: This keeps one canonical rule for the low-risk one-round bucket, resolves the current doc drift, and preserves the stronger three-round path for high-risk work without touching runtime behavior.

preMortem.scenario: The low-risk bucket becomes broader than intended.
preMortem.trigger: The new wording is read as any compliance-related work instead of wording-only annotation cleanup.
preMortem.consequence: Readers may think unrelated lifecycle or gate changes also qualify for one-round treatment.
preMortem.mitigation: Define the bucket narrowly as wording-only / annotation-compliance / pure typo doc edits and explicitly exclude lifecycle, gate, Authority, and process-fact work.

preMortem.scenario: The canonical doc and runbooks drift again.
preMortem.trigger: Only one document gets the new wording, or the adjacent runbooks keep the old phrasing.
preMortem.consequence: story_review will still flag the policy as inconsistent and the rule will remain confusing.
preMortem.mitigation: Update all touched docs in the same change and make the runbooks point back to the canonical rule in story-lifecycle.md.

preMortem.scenario: The new wording is mistaken for a runtime or Authority change.
preMortem.trigger: The audit policy text sits near Authority language and does not separate local Non-authority guidance from receipt-backed completion.
preMortem.consequence: Users may infer Authority Server proof or gate semantics changed when only docs changed.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep the text explicitly docs-only, preserve the local Non-authority framing, and state that no Authority Server completion is claimed.
